results.notes: The annual funding allocation spreadsheet shows the amount of Official Languages in Education Programs funding each school authority offering French second-language instruction will receive. Funding amounts are based on student Full-time Equivalent enrolment calculations, as detailed in Section F of the funding manual. The spreadsheet is published annually in the spring. Francophone regional authorities determine how their block of funding is distributed among the four regional authorities.

results.name: student-support-policy-framework
results.notes: The Student Support Policy Framework (SSPF) establishes a consistent provincial approach to student supports and services by providing common definitions, expectations, and guidance for school authorities across Alberta. It outlines a continuum of universal, targeted, and individualized supports, grounded in student-centred, evidence-informed, and collaborative practices to help all students succeed. The framework also clarifies roles and responsibilities, promotes accountability and continuous improvement, and strengthens coordination among schools, families, community partners, and government ministries to support student learning and well-being.

results.name: aip
results.notes: The Alberta Immunization Policy outlines the policies for the provision of publicly-funded immunizations in Alberta. It contains a complete listing of vaccines and biologicals that are publicly-funded and indications for their use.  PLEASE NOTE: These policies and documents are revised as new research and national recommendations become available. Please ensure you are always referencing the current version of the document. Check this page regularly for updates. The Canadian Immunization Guide recommendations should be consulted when further information about immunization is required.
results.subject: Immunization--Government policy--Alberta
results.title: Alberta immunization policy
results.usageconsiderations: The Alberta Immunization Policy (the "Document") and its contents may be incorporated into the working knowledge of the reader, but its use is predicated upon the professional judgment of the user that the Document is correct and is appropriate in the circumstances of particular use. The Document is provided "as is" without warranties or conditions of any kind either expressed or implied. The Document is subject to change and the Government of Alberta reserves the right to periodically update the information in the Document. It is necessary that you ensure that the version of the Document being consulted is the most current version available as of that date. Reference to or mention of specific products, trademarks, trade names, processes or services does not constitute or imply a recommendation or endorsement by the Government of Alberta. Public health and other professionals providing publicly-funded vaccines are encouraged to seek advice from Alberta’s Chief Medical Officer of Health/designate where necessary.
